title: The Ninth at the Stadium: Baker Makes a Ten, Williams Keeps the Trophy
title_candidates: The Ninth at the Stadium: Baker Makes a Ten, Williams Keeps the Trophy
Catalonia's Cruellest Yard: Williams Bleeds 14 Shots and Wins Anyway
Fifty-Nine Holes in Front, Two Holes Behind: Williams Survives Baker
Nine Shots Melt to Five: The Trophy Decided on the Hardest Hole in Spain
theme: A nine-shot lead built in one record round, spent over three days, and settled in the space of two holes on the Stadium's front nine — where the same hole handed Williams the Trophy and Mullin the Jacket.
opening_hook: Open on Act I: Williams's R1 -12 at PGA Catalunya Tour, the best round in TEG history to date (b07), and the nine-shot cushion that looked like a formality — with a nod that all of it would come down to a single par 4 on the final afternoon.
foreshadow: Williams's R1 -12 (b07) is the best round in TEG history to date and opens a nine-shot lead — a cushion that only ever shrinks.
Baker arrives with one prior Trophy win and runner-up finishes in three of the last four TEGs: the man always within touching distance.
Mullin arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 5) with back-to-back Jacket wins — a man who can win the gross prize while losing everything else.
Meller arrives with two prior Wooden Spoons and, in R2, posts the best round of his TEG life.

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, +0, by 5 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Williams took the lead on R1 H2 and led at the end of every round: -12 in R1 (b07, the best round in TEG history to date) for a nine-shot cushion, level par net in R2 (lead still 9), +3 in R3 (lead 8). Then the Stadium: he bled 13 shots across holes 6-9 (b22) and after 59 holes in front the lead was gone, Baker taking it outright at R4 H7 (b01, b04). One hole later it came back — Williams took a triple bogey at the 9th, SI 1, and still moved back to outright first (b06) because Baker had signed for a 10 there (b12). Williams then bled a further 14 shots over the closing five holes (b19), but Baker's own quadruple bogey at the 18th (b43) meant the margin held. Final: +0, by 5 (b03) — back-to-back Trophies for the defending champion.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +85, by 4 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin took the gross lead on R1 H3 and held it for 51 holes on rounds of +17 and +17. R3 at El Prat undid it: his worst gross round to date, +29 (b21), including a 9 at the 15th — his worst hole to par (b18) — and he lost the lead to Baker on the final green of the round (b02, b11). He answered on the Stadium's 9th, a par on SI 1 to retake the outright lead (b05) as Baker ran up a 10 at the same hole (b12), part of a three-hole run of pars from 8-10 (b41). Baker drew level again at H16 (b24) before an 8 at the 18th (b43) settled it. Mullin's fourth Jacket, +85 by 4 (b08).

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Meller was bottom after R1 (+7), then produced the best round of his TEG career in R2 at Costa Brava — a personal-best -5 net and personal-best +17 gross (b13, b14) — which lifted him off the foot of the table and left Neumann there instead. It lasted exactly one round: at El Prat he took a 10 at the opening par 5 to drop straight back to the bottom (b27, b44), added a 10 at the 8th, SI 2 (b17) and a 9 at the 17th, SI 1 (b28) for +15, and never climbed out. A +13 R4 confirmed it: +30 and a third Wooden Spoon (b23).

headline_candidates: The Ninth at the Stadium: One Hole, Two Titles, One Ten
Williams Drops 27 Shots in a Round and Still Wins the Trophy
Fifty-Nine Holes in Front, Then Two Holes That Decided the Lot
rounds.chosen_headline: The Ninth at the Stadium: One Hole, Two Titles, One Ten
rounds.angle: Spain's premier course takes 13 shots off Williams from the 6th to the 9th and Baker leads the Trophy outright at H7 (b01, b04) — then Baker makes a 10 at the 9th (b12), the hardest hole on the card, handing the Trophy back to a triple-bogeying Williams (b06) and the Jacket back to a par-making Mullin (b05); Baker's closing 8 at the 18th (b43) seals both defeats.

players.arc: Defending champion who opened with the best round in TEG history to date (-12, plus a personal-best +20 gross) and then spent 63 holes handing it back — 13 shots gone from the 6th to the 9th on the final day, 14 more over the closing five — before a triple bogey at the Stadium's 9th somehow restored his lead and delivered back-to-back Trophies at +0, all while finishing well adrift in the gross he has never won.

The perennial near-man led the Jacket after R3 and the Trophy outright at R4 H7, then made a 10 at the 9th and an 8 at the 18th and finished runner-up in both — beaten by five and by four respectively.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder turns his back-to-back Jackets into three in a row and a fourth overall, despite posting his worst gross round to date (+29) and his worst hole to par (a 9 at El Prat's 15th) in the middle of it, reclaiming the lead with a par at the hardest hole on the last day.

Produced the best round of his TEG life at Costa Brava and the worst 18 holes of anyone's tournament at El Prat 24 hours later — two 10s and a 9 in one round — and collected a third Wooden Spoon at +30.

Quietly held the middle of the table but bookended his tournament with blow-ups — a 9 at the 9th in R1 and a 10 at the 3rd inside a 12-shot bleed at the Stadium — and briefly wore the Spoon position after R2.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to Catalonia, Spain, and all four courses are new to every player — no course history exists anywhere in this tournament, which is itself worth a line: the record round in R1 was posted on a layout nobody had seen. Frame the four days as a sequence of escalating tests: PGA Catalunya's Tour course (the 'slightly more forgiving' sibling) yielding a TEG record; Costa Brava's technical tree-lined front nine as the day of attrition; El Prat's Rosa, Greg Norman-designed and a multiple Spanish Open host, as the day the field was dismantled; and the Stadium — Spain's premier course, European Tour-designed — as the venue that decided both the Trophy and the Jacket on its 9th hole, SI 1.
course_history_notes: Every entry in the bundle's player_course_history is a first visit: no player had seen PGA Catalunya Tour, Costa Brava, El Prat - Rosa or the Stadium before TEG 6.
Williams's best round in TEG history to date (-12, +20 gross) came on a course he was seeing for the first time.
Mullin's four gross scores across the new courses — 89, 90, 101, 94 — bracket both his best days and his worst gross round to date (+29 at El Prat).
No prior TEG has been played in Catalonia, so all four course records set here are baselines rather than benchmarks.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H9 at PGA Catalunya Stadium (SI 1) — Williams takes a triple bogey and still regains the outright lead (b06) because Baker signs for a 10 at the same hole (b12); the final five-shot margin traces to that one green.

Green Jacket: R4 H9 — Mullin's par on the hardest hole reclaims the gross lead he had lost on R3 H18 after 51 holes in front (b05, b02), and Baker's quadruple bogey 8 at the 18th (b43) ends the level-pegging he had restored at H16 (b24).
Wooden Spoon: R3 H1 at El Prat - Rosa — Meller's 10 at the opening par 5 drops him straight back to the bottom (b27, b44) and he stays there for the remaining 53 holes.
